name: Thai Song
confidence_why: One first-hand description of the tone system, checked against the source; 9 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

new_statements.quote: All the languages dealt with here (W B R S) have, in addition to the types of syllables already described, other syllables having weak stress, usually prefixed to a normal syllable. Such weak syllables usually have a short a vowel, though sometimes other vowels occur. The tone on such syllables tends to be neutralized to a mid level pitch in all four languages. [...] It is noteworthy that of the four languages here studied, Siamese has by far the greatest number of such weak syllables, Red Tai somewhat fewer, Black Tai still fewer, and in White Tai they are infrequent.
new_statements.citation: Gedney, William J. 1989 [1964]. A comparative sketch of White, Black and Red Tai. In R. J. Bickner, J. Hartmann, T. J. Hudak & P. Peyasantiwong (eds.), Selected Papers on Comparative Tai Studies (Michigan Papers on South and Southeast Asia 29), pp. 415-461. Ann Arbor: Center for South and Southeast Asian Studies, University of Michigan. [Originally Social Science Review, special number 14 (1964): 1-47.]
new_statements.locator: p. 421 (section TONES, end of the Red Tai tone list, just before 'Comparison of tones'); PDF page 7; scanned in lines 328-341, verified against the page scan
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: The passage is on p. 421 of Gedney 1989 [1964] exactly as quoted (checked against the rendered page scan of p. 7 of; the scanned textof; the elided middle sentence is Gedney's note that the phenomenon is 'so infrequent in the type of words that we are dealing with' that he marks it with a breve, e.g. S maphraaw4 'coconut'). The p. 418 remark that transcriptions are of syllables 'as pronounced in isolation' is also there. On the identity of the variety: Not OK for thai1259. Gedney (pp. 415-418) states his Black Tai data come from a family from Muang Piang (44 km NW of Son La) met at Tung Nghia, South Vietnam, and from Bac Cam So of Ban Chieng Di (35 km NW of Son La) in Vientiane, i.e.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Black Tai words consist of full ('normal') tone-bearing syllables; the only unstressed syllables are reduced presyllables (short a, tone neutralised to mid) that precede a full syllable, so in a sesqui-/disyllabic word of this type prominence is on the final, full syllable. Black Tai has few such weak presyllables (fewer than Siamese or Red Tai). No rule is given for compounds of two full syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: Weak syllables 'sometimes' have vowels other than short a; phenomenon said to be infrequent in Black Tai and to need fuller analysis per language.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; transcriptions are of syllables 'as pronounced in isolation' (p. 418), i.e. citation forms; Gedney notes connected speech has further modifications. Variety described is Black Tai (Tai Dam) of Son La speakers recorded among refugees in South Vietnam/Vientiane, i.e. the parent variety of Thai Song, not Thai Song as spoken in Thailand.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Gedney 1964/1989 p. 421) describes Black Tai = Tai Dam as spoken by Son La (NW Vietnam) speakers, Glottolog taid1247 (ISO blt), the parent variety from which the Thai Song (thai1259, ISO soa) communities of Phetchaburi etc. descend (migrated c. 200 years ago from Muang Thaeng). Burusphat 2012 treats 'Thai Song or Tai Dam (Black Tai)' as one language (codes soa, blt). Every Thai Song-specific description that could be opened (Burusphat 2011, 2012, 2013; Yensamut 1981 [Samut Sakhon]; Jirananthanaporn 2007 [Phitsanulok]) is silent on stress, so the catalog entry, if made, should be flagged as resting on a Tai Dam (Vietnam) proxy pending Maneewong 1987 or Burusphat 2013.

tone_statements.citation: สุพิดา เกิดอู่ม [Supida Koed-um]. 2561 [2018]. สำเนียงภาษาไทยโซ่ง จังหวัดเพชรบุรี (Thai Song accents of Phetchaburi Province). วารสารวจนะ / Vacana Journal of Language and Linguistics (Mae Fah Luang University) 6(1): 1-20. In Thai with English abstract. [Part of the author's MA thesis, Thammasat University, 2017.]
tone_statements.quote: The results of this study show tonal splits and coalescences pattern of Thai Song in the 7 districts are ABCD123-4; DLDS123 and DLDS4 merge with B123 and B4 respectively and all have 6 tones: Tone 1, A123 lower mid-rising; Tone 2, A4 lower mid-rising-falling; Tone 3, B123 lower mid-high rising; Tone 4, B4 mid-level; Tone 5, C123 lower mid-rising glottalized and Tone 6, C4 mid-falling glottalized. The results of the tonal system comparison between Thai Song and Tai Dam reveal that both languages have the same tonal splits and coalescence patterns, and the number of tones.
tone_statements.locator: English abstract, p. 2; Thai abstract p. 1; full statement in sec. 4.1.1-4.1.2 (ผลการวิจัย), pp. 8-9 with Table 2 (tone box) and Fig. 3.
tone_statements.summary: Six lexical syllable tones from a two-way ABCD123-4 split (checked-syllable tones = B allotones), five contour and one level, both C tones glottalised; identical system in all seven Phetchaburi districts.

tone_statements.citation: โสภิตา ถาวร และ สมทรง บุรุษพัฒน์ [Sopita Thavorn & Somsonge Burusphat]. 2561 [2018]. การใช้เกณฑ์ทางภาษาศาสตร์จัดกลุ่มย่อยภาษาไทดำและข้อสนับสนุนการอพยพย้ายถิ่นฐาน (Linguistic classification of Tai Dam dialects and immigration support). วารสารภาษาและวัฒนธรรม / Journal of Language and Culture 37(2): 61-85. In Thai with English abstract.
tone_statements.quote: ...ภาษาไทดำถิ่นต่างๆ ยังมีการเปลี่ยนแปลงเสียงวรรณยุกต์ในภาษาไทดำดั้งเดิมมาเป็นระบบวรรณยุกต์ 6 หน่วยเสียง ในภาษาไทดำปัจจุบันทุกถิ่นเป็นไปตามระบบภาษาไทดำ โดยมีการแยกเสียงรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์เป็นระบบเดียวกันคือ ABCD123-4 และ B=D ... ไทดำประเทศไทย ถิ่นบ้านหัวเขาจีน จังหวัดราชบุรี สัทลักษณะของวรรณยุกต์ A มีการเปลี่ยนแปลงไปจากเดิม โดยวรรณยุกต์ A123 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น [23] และวรรณยุกต์ A4 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น-ตก [232~243] ... ส่วนไทดำประเทศไทย ถิ่นบ้านนาป่าหนาด จังหวัดเลย วรรณยุกต์ A123 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น-ตก [242] ซึ่งแตกต่างไปจากไทดำในถิ่นอื่น ๆ ทั้งหมด
tone_statements.translation: ...the various Tai Dam dialects have all changed the Proto-Tai-Dam tones into a system of 6 tonemes; every present-day Tai Dam locality follows the Tai Dam system, with the same pattern of tone splits and mergers, ABCD123-4 and B=D ... Tai Dam of Thailand, Ban Hua Khao Chin, Ratchaburi: the phonetic shape of tone A has changed from the original, tone A123 being lower-mid rising [23] and tone A4 lower-mid rising-falling [232~243] ... whereas in Tai Dam of Thailand, Ban Na Pa Nat, Loei, tone A123 is lower-mid rising-falling [242], which differs from Tai Dam in all other localities.
tone_statements.locator: p. 71, section 5.1 การใช้เกณฑ์พัฒนาการของเสียงวรรณยุกต์ดั้งเดิม; full tone values in ตารางที่ 3, p. 66
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Six tonemes (split ABCD123-4, B=D) in all Tai Dam; Thailand varieties differ in tone A: Ratchaburi [23]/[232~243], Loei [242]. No stress.

tone_statements.citation: สุพิดา เกิดอู่ม [Supida Kerdoum]. 2560 [2017]. การเปลี่ยนแปลงเสียงวรรณยุกต์ภาษาไทยโซ่งจังหวัดเพชรบุรี (A tonal change of Thai Song in Phetchaburi). MA thesis (ศิลปศาสตรมหาบัณฑิต, ภาษาศาสตร์เพื่อการสื่อสาร), Faculty of Liberal Arts, Thammasat University; advisor นันทนา รณเกียรติ [Nantana Ronakiat]. 12 + 81 leaves. In Thai. DOI 10.14457/TU.the.2017.1668.
tone_statements.quote: The results of this study showed tonal splits and coalescence patterns in Thai Song across the 7 districts for ABCD123-4; DLDS123 and DLDS4 merged with B123 and B4 respectively and all had 6 tones: Tone 1, A123 low rising [13]; Tone 2, A4 lower-mid rising falling [243]; Tone 3, B123 low rising high [15]; Tone 4, B4 lower-mid level [22]; Tone 5, C123 lower-mid falling glottalized [21ʔ] and Tone 6, C4 mid falling glottalized [31ʔ]. Furthermore, the results also showed a tonal variation of tone 2 (A4) which was lower-mid rising [24, 25, 35] and two tonal variants of tone 4 (B4) ...
tone_statements.locator: same statement in Thai abstract p. (1) and sec. 4.1-4.2, pp. 52-55
tone_statements.summary: Six tones (split ABCD123-4); dead-syllable DL/DS tones are allotones of B123/B4; Gedney checklist by ear plus Praat F0, 14 speakers in 7 districts; A4/B4 variants attributed to contact. No stress.

tone_statements.citation: สมทรง บุรุษพัฒน์ [Somsonge Burusphat]. 2556 [2013]. การแปรและการเปลี่ยนแปลงวรรณยุกต์ไทดำ (Tonal variation and change of Tai Dam). วารสารภาษาและวัฒนธรรม / Journal of Language and Culture (RILCA, Mahidol University) 32(2): 19-41. In Thai with English abstract.
tone_statements.quote: This study of social and regional tone variation and change in Tai Dam shows an agreement of tonal systems, i.e., all varieties have six tones in live syllables. From the five tone categories of the parent language referred to as A, B, C, DL and DS, two series of tones have developed in Tai Dam varieties in all locations. Splits that have developed are ABCD123-4. DL and DS have merged with each other and DLDS123 and DLDS 4 correspond to B123 and B4 respectively. [...] A123 lower-mid falling rising; A4 lower-mid rising falling; B123 lower-mid falling rising high; B4 mid level; C123 lower-mid falling glottalized; and C4 mid falling glottalized.
tone_statements.locator: English abstract, p. 20; restated in Thai in sec. 4.1 'การแยกเสียงและรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์', p. 25 ('..จำนวนวรรณยุกต์เท่ากันทั้งหมด คือ 6 วรรณยุกต์.. ABCD123-4') and sec. 4.2, pp. 26 ff.
tone_statements.summary: Six lexical tones on the syllable in live syllables (split ABCD123-4; checked syllables carry allotones of B123/B4), five contour + one level, C tones glottalised; system uniform across regions and generations, phonetic values vary.

tone_statements.citation: เพ็ญวิภา อยู่เย็น [Penwipa Yooyen]. 2556 [2013]. การแปรเสียงวรรณยุกต์ตามตัวแปรอายุในภาษาไทยโซ่ง จังหวัดราชบุรี (Tone variation of Thai Song by age group in Ratchaburi province). MA thesis (Linguistics), Mahidol University. In Thai with English abstract.
tone_statements.quote: It is found that the tone system of Thai Song at the study area splits and merges in the same manner as the original pattern, that is, ABCD123-4. There are six tonemes as follows. Tone 1 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-low-mid low [212] Tone 2 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-mid-mid low [232] Tone 3 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-low-mid high [214] Tone 4 with the phonetic aspects of mid level [33] Tone 5 with the phonetic aspects of mid-low and glottalized [31ʔ] Tone 6 with the phonetic aspects of mid level-low and glottalized [331ʔ]
tone_statements.locator: Extended Summary, sec. 4.1 'The tone system of Thai Song at Don Khlang Sub-District', thesis p.128; same system in Thai in Table 4.1, thesis p.68
tone_statements.summary: Six tonemes, Gedney pattern ABCD123-4; five contour, tone 4 level (p.69); dead syllables DS/DL [213],[22] grouped with tones 3,4; Praat F0 by age; tone 2 shifting [232]>[24] in youth. No stress info.

tone_statements.citation: สมทรง บุรุษพัฒน์ [Somsonge Burusphat]. 2556 [2013]. การแปรและการเปลี่ยนแปลงเสียงในภาษาไทยโซ่ง (Phonological variation and change in Thai Song). Research report, RILCA, Mahidol University. 215 pp. (Thai)
tone_statements.quote: ภาษาไทยโซ่งทั้ง 8 ถิ่นก็เช่นกันได้มีการรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์ทําให้ภาษาไทยโซ่งทุกถิ่นที่ศึกษามีจํานวนวรรณยุกต์เท่ากันทั้งหมดคือ 6 วรรณยุกต์ ... [English abstract:] Despite the phonetic variation of tones, the six representative phonetic features of tones are determined based on the most frequency of usages: A123 mid falling rising; A4 mid rising falling; B123 lower mid falling high rising; B4 mid level; C123 lower-mid falling with glottalized; and C4 mid falling with glottalized.
tone_statements.translation: The 8 Thai Song localities likewise have undergone tone mergers, so that every Thai Song locality studied has the same number of tones, namely 6 tones ... (second part is English in the original).
tone_statements.locator: ch. 5 sec. 5.1, p. 90 + English abstract p. ข; six-tone list restated ch. 6 pp. 122-123
tone_statements.summary: Six tones in live syllables (Gedney boxes, split ABCD123-4, DL/DS merged with B); dead syllables carry allotones of tones 3 and 4; Praat F0 on 80 words, 3 age groups x 8 villages; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: สุนทรัตร์ แสงงาม [Suntharat Saeng-ngam]. 2549 [2006]. การแปรของคำศัพท์และวรรณยุกต์ตามกลุ่มอายุและทัศนคติต่อภาษาในภาษาโซ่ง (ไทดำ) ที่พูดในอำเภอเขาย้อย จังหวัดเพชรบุรี (Lexical and tonal variation by age group and language attitude in the Song language (Black Tai) of Amphoe Khao Yoi, Changwat Phetchaburi). MA thesis (Linguistics), Faculty of Arts, Chulalongkorn University. 183 pp. (PDF). In Thai.
tone_statements.quote: หลังจากผู้วิจัยได้วิเคราะห์ระบบวรรณยุกต์ของผู้บอกภาษาทั้งหมด 32 คน จาก 3 กลุ่มอายุในตำบลหนองปรง อำเภอเขาย้อย พบว่าภาษาโซ่งที่พูดที่ตำบลนี้มีระบบวรรณยุกต์ที่ใช้กันทั่วไป เป็นระบบวรรณยุกต์แบบ 6 หน่วยเสียง (ดูภาพที่ 5.1) ประกอบด้วยหน่วยเสียงดังนี้ หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 1 กลาง-ขึ้น หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 2 ต่ำ-ขึ้น-ตก หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 3 ต่ำ-ขึ้น หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 4 กลาง-ระดับ หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 5 ต่ำ-ระดับ หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 6 กลาง-ตก
tone_statements.translation: After analysing the tone systems of all 32 speakers from 3 age groups in Tambon Nong Prong, Amphoe Khao Yoi, it was found that the Song language spoken in this subdistrict has one generally used tone system, a 6-toneme system (see Fig. 5.1), consisting of: toneme 1 mid-rising; toneme 2 low-rising-falling; toneme 3 low-rising; toneme 4 mid-level; toneme 5 low-level; toneme 6 mid-falling.
tone_statements.locator: thesis p. 70, ch. 5 sec. 5.1.1 'ระบบวรรณยุกต์'; tone-box split sec. 5.1.2, p. 71, Table 5.1.
tone_statements.summary: Six lexical syllable tones (mid-rising, low-rising-falling, low-rising, mid-level, low-level, mid-falling) with the A B C 123-4 split; phonetic variation by age group and language attitude.

tone_statements.citation: วิไลลักษณ์ เดชะ [Wilailuck Daecha]. 2530 [1987; academic year 2529/1986]. ศึกษาเปรียบเทียบระบบเสียงของภาษาไท(ย) 6 ภาษาที่พูดในอำเภอท่าตะโก จังหวัดนครสวรรค์ (A comparative study of the phonology of six Tai dialects spoken in Amphoe Tha Tako, Changwat Nakhon Sawan: Lao Tai, Lao Wiang, Lao Khrang, Lao Ngaew, Phuan, Song). MA thesis (Linguistics), Chulalongkorn University; advisor Theraphan L. Thongkum.
tone_statements.quote: Regarding tonal system, Song has 6 tones, whereas the others have only 5 tones. [...] The differences are that the other dialects have initial aspirated stops but Song has initial unaspirated stops, and the development of tones from proto tones is ABCD 123-4, but the Lao group (Lao Tai, Lao Wiang, Lao Krang, and Lao Ngaew) has AC 1-234, B=DL, and Phuan has A 1-234, B=DL and there is no split in the C column.
tone_statements.locator: English abstract, front matter; full treatment ch. 5 'tones', Lao Song pp. 86-90.
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Song of Tha Tako has six lexical tones with the ABCD123-4 split (the neighbouring Lao and Phuan dialects have five).

sources.quote: The results of this study show tonal splits and coalescences pattern of Thai Song in the 7 districts are ABCD123-4; DLDS123 and DLDS4 merge with B123 and B4 respectively and all have 6 tones: Tone 1, A123 lower mid-rising; Tone 2, A4 lower mid-rising-falling; Tone 3, B123 lower mid-high rising; Tone 4, B4 mid-level; Tone 5, C123 lower mid-rising glottalized and Tone 6, C4 mid-falling glottalized. The results of the tonal system comparison between Thai Song and Tai Dam reveal that both languages have the same tonal splits and coalescence patterns, and the number of tones.

sources.quote: ...ภาษาไทดำถิ่นต่างๆ ยังมีการเปลี่ยนแปลงเสียงวรรณยุกต์ในภาษาไทดำดั้งเดิมมาเป็นระบบวรรณยุกต์ 6 หน่วยเสียง ในภาษาไทดำปัจจุบันทุกถิ่นเป็นไปตามระบบภาษาไทดำ โดยมีการแยกเสียงรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์เป็นระบบเดียวกันคือ ABCD123-4 และ B=D ... ไทดำประเทศไทย ถิ่นบ้านหัวเขาจีน จังหวัดราชบุรี สัทลักษณะของวรรณยุกต์ A มีการเปลี่ยนแปลงไปจากเดิม โดยวรรณยุกต์ A123 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น [23] และวรรณยุกต์ A4 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น-ตก [232~243] ... ส่วนไทดำประเทศไทย ถิ่นบ้านนาป่าหนาด จังหวัดเลย วรรณยุกต์ A123 มีเสียงเป็นกลางต่ำ-ขึ้น-ตก [242] ซึ่งแตกต่างไปจากไทดำในถิ่นอื่น ๆ ทั้งหมด

tone.translation: ...the various Tai Dam dialects have all changed the Proto-Tai-Dam tones into a system of 6 tonemes; every present-day Tai Dam locality follows the Tai Dam system, with the same pattern of tone splits and mergers, ABCD123-4 and B=D ... Tai Dam of Thailand, Ban Hua Khao Chin, Ratchaburi: the phonetic shape of tone A has changed from the original, tone A123 being lower-mid rising [23] and tone A4 lower-mid rising-falling [232~243] ... whereas in Tai Dam of Thailand, Ban Na Pa Nat, Loei, tone A123 is lower-mid rising-falling [242], which differs from Tai Dam in all other localities.

sources.citation: สมทรง บุรุษพัฒน์ [Somsonge Burusphat]. 2556 [2013]. การแปรและการเปลี่ยนแปลงวรรณยุกต์ไทดำ (Tonal variation and change of Tai Dam). วารสารภาษาและวัฒนธรรม / Journal of Language and Culture (RILCA, Mahidol University) 32(2): 19-41. In Thai with English abstract.
sources.quote: This study of social and regional tone variation and change in Tai Dam shows an agreement of tonal systems, i.e., all varieties have six tones in live syllables. From the five tone categories of the parent language referred to as A, B, C, DL and DS, two series of tones have developed in Tai Dam varieties in all locations. Splits that have developed are ABCD123-4. DL and DS have merged with each other and DLDS123 and DLDS 4 correspond to B123 and B4 respectively. [...] A123 lower-mid falling rising; A4 lower-mid rising falling; B123 lower-mid falling rising high; B4 mid level; C123 lower-mid falling glottalized; and C4 mid falling glottalized.
sources.locator: English abstract, p. 20; restated in Thai in sec. 4.1 'การแยกเสียงและรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์', p. 25 ('..จำนวนวรรณยุกต์เท่ากันทั้งหมด คือ 6 วรรณยุกต์.. ABCD123-4') and sec. 4.2, pp. 26 ff.
sources.note: Gedney-box tone study (auditory + acoustic) of Thai Song/Tai Dam in four Thai provinces by age group: all varieties and all generations share one system of six tones in live syllables from a two-way split ABCD123-4; DL=DS, and DLDS123/DLDS4 pattern with B123/B4 (checked syllables); representative values A123 lower-mid falling-rising [213 etc.], A4 lower-mid rising-falling, B123 lower-mid falling-rising-high, B4 mid level [33], C123 lower-mid falling glottalised [21ʔ], C4 mid falling glottalised; phonetic variants by age/region tabulated (sec. 4.2, table pp. 26 ff.); some young speakers lose C…

sources.quote: It is found that the tone system of Thai Song at the study area splits and merges in the same manner as the original pattern, that is, ABCD123-4. There are six tonemes as follows. Tone 1 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-low-mid low [212] Tone 2 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-mid-mid low [232] Tone 3 with the phonetic aspects of mid low-low-mid high [214] Tone 4 with the phonetic aspects of mid level [33] Tone 5 with the phonetic aspects of mid-low and glottalized [31ʔ] Tone 6 with the phonetic aspects of mid level-low and glottalized [331ʔ]

tone.translation: After analysing the tone systems of all 32 speakers from 3 age groups in Tambon Nong Prong, Amphoe Khao Yoi, it was found that the Song language spoken in this subdistrict has one generally used tone system, a 6-toneme system (see Fig. 5.1), consisting of: toneme 1 mid-rising; toneme 2 low-rising-falling; toneme 3 low-rising; toneme 4 mid-level; toneme 5 low-level; toneme 6 mid-falling.
tone.summary: Six lexical syllable tones (mid-rising, low-rising-falling, low-rising, mid-level, low-level, mid-falling) with the A B C 123-4 split; phonetic variation by age group and language attitude.
tone.says: Ch. 5 (pp. 69 ff.): auditory + acoustic (Praat) analysis of 32 speakers in three age groups: the Song of Nong Prong has a 6-toneme system - T1 mid-rising, T2 low-rising-falling, T3 low-rising, T4 mid-level, T5 low-level, T6 mid-falling - with the 'traditional' split A B C 123-4 (sec. 5.1.2, citing Panka 2523 and Liamprawat 2541); 13 further speakers showed an apparent B4=C4 merger (5 tones) that the author set aside as a data problem; secs. 5.2 ff. give per-tone F0 variants by age and attitude.…

sources.citation: วิไลลักษณ์ เดชะ [Wilailuck Daecha]. 2530 [1987; academic year 2529/1986]. ศึกษาเปรียบเทียบระบบเสียงของภาษาไท(ย) 6 ภาษาที่พูดในอำเภอท่าตะโก จังหวัดนครสวรรค์ (A comparative study of the phonology of six Tai dialects spoken in Amphoe Tha Tako, Changwat Nakhon Sawan: Lao Tai, Lao Wiang, Lao Khrang, Lao Ngaew, Phuan, Song). MA thesis (Linguistics), Chulalongkorn University; advisor Theraphan L. Thongkum.
sources.quote: Regarding tonal system, Song has 6 tones, whereas the others have only 5 tones. [...] The differences are that the other dialects have initial aspirated stops but Song has initial unaspirated stops, and the development of tones from proto tones is ABCD 123-4, but the Lao group (Lao Tai, Lao Wiang, Lao Krang, and Lao Ngaew) has AC 1-234, B=DL, and Phuan has A 1-234, B=DL and there is no split in the C column.
sources.locator: English abstract, front matter; full treatment ch. 5 'tones', Lao Song pp. 86-90.
sources.note: English abstract: consonants, vowels and tones of six Tai dialects compared; 'Song has 6 tones, whereas the others have only 5 tones'; Song's tonal development from proto-tones is ABCD 123-4 (vs. Lao group A C 1-234, B=DL; Phuan A 1-234, B=DL, no C split). Ch. 5 (pp. 86-90, not held by the project) gives the Song tone inventory with values.

tone.quote: ภาษาไทยโซ่งทั้ง 8 ถิ่นก็เช่นกันได้มีการรวมเสียงของวรรณยุกต์ทําให้ภาษาไทยโซ่งทุกถิ่นที่ศึกษามีจํานวนวรรณยุกต์เท่ากันทั้งหมดคือ 6 วรรณยุกต์ ... [English abstract:] Despite the phonetic variation of tones, the six representative phonetic features of tones are determined based on the most frequency of usages: A123 mid falling rising; A4 mid rising falling; B123 lower mid falling high rising; B4 mid level; C123 lower-mid falling with glottalized; and C4 mid falling with glottalized.

tone.translation: The 8 Thai Song localities likewise have undergone tone mergers, so that every Thai Song locality studied has the same number of tones, namely 6 tones ... (second part is English in the original).
tone.summary: Six tones in live syllables (Gedney boxes, split ABCD123-4, DL/DS merged with B); dead syllables carry allotones of tones 3 and 4; Praat F0 on 80 words, 3 age groups x 8 villages; nothing on stress.
